MG11_POSSIBLE_TEXT: Sex without protection on these days can lead to pregnancy. For a healthy couple trying for a baby, the chance is about 1 in 4 or 5 per cycle.
MG11_UNLIKELY_TEXT: But cycles vary: ovulation can come earlier or later, and sperm can live up to 5 days. That's why protection matters every day.
MG11_AFTER1: Six fertile days in every cycle: the five before ovulation and the day itself.
MG11_AFTER2: They don't come with a sign on them. If you don't want a baby, protection every time is the safe bet.

PREROD_LUTEUM: What stays behind becomes the corpus luteum, the yellow body. It makes progesterone.
CAVE_PHASE_SUB: Day one of the cycle. The uterus sheds the lining it didn't need: that is your period.
RUN_PHASE_SUB: The period ends, estrogen rises. In the ovary a follicle, a tiny sac with an egg, ripens: your sun.
PMS_PHASE_SUB: After ovulation progesterone takes over. Late in the phase the hormones drop, and PMS may come.
END_PHASE_1: Your period is the uterus shedding its lining: rest, warmth and iron-rich food help.
END_PHASE_2: Estrogen rises and an egg ripens in its follicle: energy and focus often grow.
END_PHASE_3: The ovary releases an egg: the few days before it and that day are the fertile ones.
END_PHASE_4: Progesterone takes over; if PMS comes before your period, rest and being kind to yourself help.
END_CLOSING: The cycle comes round again, and now you know it.
END_NOTE: Every body has its own rhythm: a cycle rarely lasts exactly 28 days.
